name: bog

attributes.attribute: formed of centuries of compacted sphagnum moss and plants
a liminal zone and entrance to the Otherworld
preserves lost or sacrificed objects due to low oxygen and tannic acid

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The bog is a symbolic site. Centuries of sphagnum moss and plants compacted in water formed it. Bogs were common in the Irish and Scottish countryside until recently. Peat from bogs is still dried into turf and burned as fuel. Turf-harvesting was labor-intensive until the mid-20th century. Mechanical harvesting destroyed vast ancient bogs. Bogs are liminal zones. They are neither dry nor wet. They resist building roads or homes. So they make perfect entrances to the Otherworld. Bogs also matter to archaeology. Low oxygen and excess tannic acid preserve lost or sacrificed objects well. Many treasures in the National Museum of Ireland come from bogs.

okr.objective: Describe the bog as a symbolic site and source of peat and archaeology.
